evidence.clarity: 1440 first screen: H1 'It fails in CI. Now it fails on your laptop too.' plus bold lede 'Rerun is a free command-line tool for backend engineers' says what, who and how. The install panel beside it holds the exact brief command and a button that says what it does ('Copy install command').
evidence.fit: Uses only the destinations the brief supplied (npm install -g @rerun/cli, rerun.example/docs, github.example/rerun/rerun). The pricing section reads 'Free and MIT-licensed. A hosted team version is planned, not built' and 'There are GitHub stars and no customer logos', which matches the brief. A 'Limits' section answers developer distrust without inventing customers. It does add capability limits not in the brief (Node-only, no child processes); these are scoping statements, not proof.

evidence.clarity: H1 'The test that only fails in CI, failing on your laptop.' and the lede 'records a failing test run in CI and replays it exactly where you can put a breakpoint in it... Free, MIT-licensed, one command to install' make the product and next step clear at 1440 and 390. The audience (backend engineers) is implied, not named.
evidence.fit: Uses the supplied install command, docs and repo. Adds footer links /issues and /docs/changelog under the supplied domains. 'Where the project stands' answers 'no company users we can name' head on. But it invents many facts the brief does not support: the support matrix (Jest, Vitest, Mocha, node --test, Node 18+, GitHub Actions/GitLab/CircleCI/Buildkite), 'Two people, part time... pull requests get a review within a week', 'adds a few hundred milliseconds', 1-5 MB recordings, secret redaction and scheduling replay. For an audience the brief says distrusts marketing, that is the wrong way to resolve the tension.
evidence.distinctiveness: A serif editorial voice plus a terminal player with a scrub bar, a red fail tick and a speed control is a coherent idea. A terminal-in-hero is still a common dev-tool pattern, and the sections below (steps, table, status dl, FAQ accordion, closing CTA) are conventional.
evidence.proof: The terminal autoplays in the first screen at 1440 (IntersectionObserver), plays to '2 passing · 1 failing · identical to CI run 4821' and 'rerun diff... 0 differ'. It is a playback, not something that responds to input beyond play/scrub/speed. It is not labelled as a sample: the note says it is 'a recording of a real replay session'. At 390 the key result lines are cut off inside the terminal.
evidence.craft: 30 KB, no assets, inline SVG favicon, system serif/mono fonts, no requests. Colour tokens exist, but spacing and type are scattered px/clamp values with no scale. Defects: player controls are 25px tall (Play 76x25, speed 38x25), range 28px. Timer bug: restarting from the end can show 't=-1:60.0' with an empty screen, because rAF timestamp < performance.now() makes dt negative, so t goes below 0 and fmt() prints -1:60.0. Reproduced at 390 in 1 of 40 restarts. Zoom 200%: 0 overflow.
evidence.mobile: 390: page overflow 0, but the terminal region scrolls sideways (sw 560 / cw 358). '(2,003 ms)', 'identical to CI ru…' and '0 differ' are cut off in B-390 end state. Player buttons are 25px tall and the speed button is 38x25. At 320 the install command is clipped at '@rer' inside its box. axe at 390: scrollable-region-focusable (serious) on #install-cmd and the closing install pre, matching probe.json. Nav links are 19px tall.
evidence.honesty: Unsupported claims are presented as fact. FAQ 'How much does recording slow down CI?': 'roughly 2-4% on the test run itself, in our measurements on Jest suites between 500 and 5,000 tests. Numbers and the benchmark script are in the repository.' The note under the demo says 'This is a recording of a real replay session... the same millisecond it failed in CI.' Also 'issues from people running it in real pipelines' and 'Issues get a reply within a few days'. The candid 'You would normally find a row of company logos here. We don't have company users we can name yet' and 'no waitlist because there is nothing to wait for yet' are good, but they sit beside invented numbers.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440/768/390. Autoplay, Pause/Play/Replay, speed 1x->2x->4x, scrub Home/End/PageDown/arrows, Space/Enter on the terminal region, Copy (clipboard verified, label flips to 'Copied' for 1.6 s) and FAQ details all work. Reduced motion jumps to the end state (17 lines, cursor animation none). Bugs: (1) the first scrub input while playing is discarded: stop() calls render(), which writes scrub.value back before the handler reads it; setting 7000 while playing left t=0:00.6, and End pressed while playing leaves t=0:00.5 until pressed again; (2) negative time '-1:60.0' on restart (above); (3) Copy feedback is not announced: no live region (0 on page), and aria-label stays 'Copy install command'; (4) the speed button's accessible name 'Playback speed' hides its visible value '1×' (label-in-name); (5) a role=region div acts as a play/pause button; (6) with JS off the terminal is an empty black box labelled 'replaying'. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Precise, readable copy: 'Three commands, start to breakpoint', 'Why not just retry the test? Retrying hides the failure until it reaches production', 'there is no waitlist because there is nothing to wait for yet'. Weakened by invented specifics and an inconsistency: the H1 promises 'failing on your laptop' while the timing claim '2,003 ms in — the same millisecond' is unverifiable marketing precision. The play button label is a default 'Play'.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: headline, lede, install + Copy, and the terminal starting to play are all in view. 390: headline, lede, install + Copy and the terminal header with 3 truncated lines. The 'real session' framing makes the in-view evidence less believable to an engineer, not more.

problems: Fabricated proof: '2-4% ... in our measurements on Jest suites between 500 and 5,000 tests' overhead figures, and the demo presented as 'a recording of a real replay session', plus invented maintainer/support/usage facts
Player bugs: the first scrub while playing snaps back, the clock can show '-1:60.0' with an empty screen on restart, and Copy success is not announced to assistive tech

hard_fail_flags.evidence: Performance numbers not supplied by the brief are presented as measured fact: FAQ answer reads 'A few hundred milliseconds of startup, and roughly 2–4% on the test run itself, in our measurements on Jest suites between 500 and 5,000 tests. Numbers and the benchmark script are in the repository.' The demo is also presented as real, not as a sample: 'This is a recording of a real replay session, played back in the page.'
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P004/B/index.html from disk at 1440x900. Scroll to 'Questions engineers ask first' and click 'How much does recording slow down CI?' to read the 2–4% claim (B/index.html line 350). The 'real replay session' sentence is the paragraph directly under the terminal (line 249).

reason: A is the page I would rather maintain and defend. Its tape artifact works through every state by mouse, touch and keyboard, and its live regions, 44px targets, tokenised CSS and no-JS fallback all hold up. Its claims stay inside the brief, and examples are labelled. B is well written but invents benchmark and usage facts, has two reproducible player bugs, unannounced copy feedback and sub-44px controls, and its terminal output is cut off at 390. A fix to B's fabricated numbers and player bugs would narrow the gap, but A's contrast and Escape issues are smaller to fix.
